title: Spanish Verb Estar Practice: Forms, Uses and Quiz with Answers
description: Practice the Spanish verb estar: present and preterite forms, its uses, ten self-correcting questions and a short reading with comprehension questions. No login.
intro: Estar is the «to be» of where things are and how they are right now: location, feelings, temporary states and actions in progress. Learn its forms, see each use with an example and practice with instant feedback.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127.csv

uses.example: Mi casa está cerca del parque.
uses.meaning: My house is near the park.

quiz.why: Location of a specific thing: está.
A feeling at a moment: estoy.
Action in progress with ellos: están + -iendo.
A temporary state of the coffee: está.
The result of an action (open) is a state: está.
A closed period (todo el día, ayer): estuve.
A completed stay with a set length: estuvieron.

paragraphs: ¡Hola, mamá! Ya estoy en el aeropuerto de Dallas. Estoy un poco cansada porque el primer vuelo salió muy temprano, pero estoy bien. Ahora estoy sentada en un café cerca de la puerta 12. El aeropuerto está lleno de gente porque mañana es Acción de Gracias.

Mi próximo vuelo está retrasado una hora. Carlos está conmigo y está comiendo una hamburguesa enorme. Te llamo cuando estemos en Phoenix. ¿Papá está en casa o todavía está en el trabajo? Dile que su regalo está en mi maleta y que está muy bien envuelto.

comprehension.before: La chica está en el aeropuerto de
comprehension.why: «Ya estoy en el aeropuerto de Dallas.»
The first flight left very early.

mistakes.wrong: La fiesta está en mi casa.
mistakes.right: La fiesta es en mi casa.
mistakes.why: Where an event happens takes ser, not estar.

mistakes.right: Estoy aburrido = I am bored; soy aburrido = I am boring.
mistakes.why: Some adjectives change meaning with ser and estar.

mistakes.wrong: Hay el libro en la mesa.
mistakes.right: El libro está en la mesa.
mistakes.why: Use hay for something new or indefinite and está for a specific thing.

heritage: If you speak Spanish at home, you probably use estar correctly every day. In writing, check the accents: estás, está and están all need one, and estoy does not. Many fluent speakers also write «estábamos» without its accent. Rewrite the airport message as if you were the mother answering, using estar at least eight times.
teacher: Teachers: the reading is a text message, a format students write every day. Ask them to underline each estar and say which use it shows (location, feeling, state, action in progress). Then they write their own message from a place they are in right now.

figure.text: On 27 November 2026, Google suggested 10 searches to people in the United States who typed «spanish verb estar». 5 of them ask for conjugation, charts or tenses (conjugation, conjugation chart, past tense, present tense, chart). This page adds practice to the forms: five uses, ten questions and a short text full of estar.
